findings.evidence: Mathlib/RingTheory/DedekindDomain/IntegralClosure.lean:145 `variable [Algebra.IsSeparable K L]`, :175 `theorem IsIntegralClosure.finite`. Roadmap provenance TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves/README.md:1091-1100 records `intermediateRingFinite` needing "nothing more" than `[Field F]`, supported by `RingTheory/IntegralClosure/NormalizationFinite` — a separability-free proof of the same statement.
findings.fix: Reword to: the hypothesis is imposed by the only Mathlib route (`IsIntegralClosure.finite`, whose section carries `[Algebra.IsSeparable K L]`, via the trace pairing, which is nondegenerate exactly for separable extensions); the inseparable case is true but needs a different argument (excellence / N-2 finiteness) and is left to later work — as the PR description itself already says.
findings.issue: "Separability is a genuine hypothesis rather than an artefact of the proof" overclaims: the justification given is entirely about the available proof route (`IsIntegralClosure.finite` via the trace pairing), and the statement is in fact true without separability — the integral closure of a finitely generated domain over a field in a finite extension of its fraction field is module-finite (Noether). Also "the trace form degenerates exactly on purely inseparable extensions" is wrong: it degenerates on every inseparable extension, not only purely inseparable ones.

findings.evidence: Finite.lean:93; same defect as the module docstring at Finite.lean:19.
findings.fix: Match the corrected module docstring: state that separability is what the Mathlib route needs, not what the result needs.
findings.issue: `moduleFinite_intermediateRing`'s docstring repeats the same overclaim ("Separability is a genuine hypothesis — see the module docstring"), so a reader of the theorem alone concludes the inseparable statement is false or open.

findings.evidence: Basic.lean:54-58 vs the new `Isogeny.moduleFinite_intermediateRing` at Finite.lean:94; the two files are siblings under `IntermediateRing/` after this PR.
findings.fix: Add one sentence naming `IntermediateRing/Finite.lean` and `moduleFinite_intermediateRing` as where the separable case now lives, keeping the note that the inseparable case remains open.
findings.issue: Basic.lean's Design section still reads "The structural theory of this ring — module-finiteness over `W₂.CoordinateRing`, and its being a Dedekind domain — is deliberately not proved here", with no pointer to the sibling `IntermediateRing/Finite.lean` this PR adds, which proves the separable case. A reader of the defining file is told the material is absent.

summary: Docstrings are otherwise accurate and well-scoped, but the file and theorem docstrings assert that separability is mathematically necessary when it is only an artefact of the one Mathlib route used, and the sibling Basic.lean is left telling readers the module-finiteness does not exist in the repo.
